scope: New references required by ProxyBehaviourEvidence.tsx. Existing canonical IDs are reused; this file does not modify the shared bibliography.

references.authors: Lundström JN, Mathe A, Schaal B, Frasnelli J, Nitzsche K, Gerber J, Hummel T
references.title: Maternal status regulates cortical responses to the body odor of newborns
references.verification: Publisher full text: 15 first-time mothers and 15 nulliparous women, unfamiliar newborn odour, fMRI; no oxytocin or reproductive decision endpoint.

references.authors: Coan JA, Schaefer HS, Davidson RJ
references.title: Lending a hand: social regulation of the neural response to threat
references.verification: Primary PubMed abstract: 16 married women, spouse/stranger/no-hand conditions, threat-related fMRI response. No hormone or reproductive outcome measured.

references.authors: Dhillo WS, Chaudhri OB, Thompson EL, Murphy KG, Patterson M, Ramachandran R, Nijher GK, Amber V, Kokkinos A, Donaldson M, Ghatei MA, Bloom SR
references.title: Kisspeptin-54 stimulates gonadotropin release most potently during the preovulatory phase of the menstrual cycle in women
references.journal: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism
references.verification: Primary abstract: eight women received 0.4 nmol/kg kisspeptin-54 or saline in random order at each cycle phase; LH response depended strongly on phase. Does not directly localise a receptor-state change or measure melatonin-to-kisspeptin coupling.

references.authors: Desmurget M, Reilly KT, Richard N, Szathmari A, Mottolese C, Sirigu A
references.title: Movement intention after parietal cortex stimulation in humans
references.verification: Primary abstract and primary article text: direct electrical stimulation during awake neurosurgery in seven patients; dissociation of intention, action and awareness. Not environmental RF or a hormone intervention.

references.authors: Gettler LT, McDade TW, Feranil AB, Kuzawa CW
references.title: Longitudinal evidence that fatherhood decreases testosterone in human males
references.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
references.verification: Primary article and existing sensory audit: longitudinal fatherhood/caregiving association, 624 men. Lower testosterone here is compatible with paternal adaptation and is not itself evidence of reproductive damage.

references.title: Reasons adults give for not having children
references.verification: Original report and Wave 147 topline checked. April 29–May 19, 2024; US adults ages 18–49 without children and unlikely to have them, n=770. 57% gave simply not wanting children as a major reason; this is not all childless adults or a biological diagnosis.
